newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal rebels kill eight woodcutters in India.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels kill eight woodcutters in India.

text.p: Tribal militants enforcing a ban on tree-cutting killed eight people and wounded 12 in three raids in northeastern India, police said on Wednesday.

Five separatist guerrillas from the Bodo Security Force, riding on motorcycles, shot the woodcutters dead on Wednesday at three spots along the border between Assam and West Bengal states, police in Calcutta said.
Authorities said the Bodos, who live in forests, were enforcing a government ban on the felling of trees. The rebels have demanded timber merchants operating in the region pay them money.
"It seems that the Bodo rebels have killed the woodcutters as punishment for not obeying the ban order and for not paying the subscription (money)," a government official said.

The Bodo Security Force wants a separate Bodo nation. A rival group, the Bodo Liberation Tigers Force, which is seeking a separate state within India, set off two bombs under a packed passenger train last month, killing at least 33 people.
The Assam state government recently asked the federal government for up to 20,000 additional paramilitary troops to help with a stepped-up counter-insurgency drive.
